title: A point outside a finite family of small events
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $\beta$ be a finite set, and assign an arbitrary subset $A_b\subseteq\Omega$ to each $b\in\beta$. If $B\in\mathbb R$ satisfies $\mu^*(A_b)\le B$ for every $b$ and $|\beta|B<1$, where $\mu^*$ is the outer measure induced by $\mu$, then there is a point of $\Omega$ belonging to none of the sets $A_b$.
replaced: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $J$ be a finite index set, and let $(A_j)_{j\in J}$ be arbitrary subsets of $\Omega$. If a real number $B$ satisfies $\mu^*(A_j)\le B$ for every $j$ and $|J|B<1$, then some $\omega\in\Omega$ belongs to none of the $A_j$, where $\mu^*$ denotes the outer measure of $\mu$.
